key_insight: A turbulence-aware model that combines multiscale volumetric reconstruction, temporal state-space modeling, and physics-based regularization can recover high-fidelity 3D turbulent flow fields from coarse data.
engineering_relevance: This enables cheaper and more practical reconstruction of detailed flow fields for CFD analysis, visualization, and downstream engineering decision-making when full-resolution simulation or measurement is unavailable.
method: Multiscale neural operator reconstructs 3D spatial flow structures from coarse-grained inputs.
State space model enforces time-resolved consistency in the reconstructed dynamics.
Navier-Stokes residuals and a mixture-of-experts module add physics guidance and adaptation to unknown coarse-graining.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on canonical turbulent systems and atmospheric reanalysis data, where it reduced reconstruction errors and better preserved multiscale structure and temporal coherence than learning-based and classical baselines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the physics residual formulation and the ability of the mixture-of-experts module to generalize to unseen coarse-graining patterns.
paper_title: High-fidelity Three-Dimensional Flow Field Reconstruction Driven by Turbulent Fluid Dynamics
